data.title: Fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, sparfloxacin, norfloxacin)
data.summary: Other antibacterials · Synthetic fluorinated quinolone antibiotics
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antibacterials_

**Class:** Synthetic fluorinated quinolone antibiotics

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II — main target in Gram-negatives) and topoisomerase IV (Gram-positives) → DNA breaks → bactericidal
- Concentration-dependent killing

## Pharmacokinetics
- Well absorbed but chelated by antacids, iron, calcium, zinc, dairy
- Good tissue and intracellular penetration; ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin/ofloxacin renally excreted; moxifloxacin hepatic

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Gram-negative skin and soft-tissue infections (Pseudomonas — ciprofloxacin), diabetic foot, osteomyelitis
- Chancroid (ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily × 3 days), donovanosis (ciprofloxacin 750 mg twice daily ≥3 weeks)
- Gonorrhoea — no longer recommended (high resistance)
- Leprosy (ofloxacin, moxifloxacin — second-line), TB (MDR regimens), rapid-growing NTM (sensitivity-guided)
- Typhoid, anthrax, rickettsial infections (alternative)

## Dose & formulations
- Ciprofloxacin 500–750 mg twice daily; ofloxacin 200–400 mg twice daily; levofloxacin 500–750 mg once daily; moxifloxacin 400 mg once daily

## Adverse effects
- Tendinopathy and tendon rupture (Achilles; risk higher with age >60, steroids, renal transplant) — FDA boxed warning, also peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, myasthenia exacerbation
- QT prolongation, dysglycaemia, aortic aneurysm/dissection
- Phototoxicity (sparfloxacin highest — withdrawn in many countries; ofloxacin least); photo-onycholysis
- Fixed drug eruption, SJS/TEN, vasculitis
- Arthropathy in growing animals → avoided in children and pregnancy (relative)
- C. difficile diarrhoea, seizures (especially with NSAIDs)

## Contraindications
- Children and adolescents (relative), pregnancy and breastfeeding (relative)
- History of tendon disorder with fluoroquinolones; myasthenia gravis; long QT

## Drug interactions
- Antacids/iron/calcium/zinc: separate by 2–6 h
- Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 → theophylline, caffeine, tizanidine toxicity
- Warfarin (INR rises), NSAIDs (seizures), steroids (tendon rupture), QT drugs

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (use only when no alternative).

## Viva points
- DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV
- Tendon rupture — boxed warning; worse with steroids
- Sparfloxacin most phototoxic, ofloxacin least
- Ciprofloxacin–theophylline interaction

_Sources: Khopkar ch.1 (Fluoroquinolones, Table 1.8); Wolverton 4e ch.9. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
